books.translationNote: Wheel of Heaven Translation from the Sumerian composite transliteration of ETCSL 1.7.4 (The Flood Story). The fragmentary Sumerian flood-narrative — the cleanest pre-Akkadian bridge to Genesis 6-9. Of an estimated ~262 original lines, only ~89 are preserved across 5 segments (A-E), with 4 large lacunae (~32, 34, 38, 33 lines missing) plus an opening lacuna of ~36 lines before Segment A. Ziusudra is the Sumerian flood-survivor (the *zi-ud-sura*, 'life of long days'); he is warned by Enki, builds a boat, survives a seven-day storm, sacrifices to An and Enlil, and is granted immortal life in Dilmun.

books.author: Wheel of Heaven Translation Program

books.author: Wheel of Heaven Translation Program
books.translationNote: Wheel of Heaven Translation of the Ugaritic Baal Cycle from Ras Shamra (ancient Ugarit, modern Latakia, Syria) — THE PROJECT'S FIRST UGARITIC-SOURCE TEXT and FIRST LEVANTINE-TRADITION TEXT. The Baal Cycle (KTU 1.1–1.6) is a six-tablet Late Bronze Age (14th–13th c. BCE) Northwest-Semitic mythological composition discovered at Ras Shamra in 1929–1931. It is the single most important comparative-mythology text for understanding Hebrew Bible motifs: Baʿlu vs Yammu (the storm-god's victory over Sea) maps onto Yahweh-vs-Yam at Psalm 74:13–14 / Psalm 89:9–10 / Isaiah 27:1 (Leviathan = Ugaritic Lôtanu); El as head-of-pantheon prefigures Hebrew El/Elohim; bn ilm = Hebrew bnei elohim (Gen 6:2, Job 1:6, Deut 32:8 LXX); Athirat = Hebrew Asherah; Mot = Hebrew mavet (death personified). Chapter 1 covers KTU 1.1 + 1.2 (Baal vs Yamm — the sea-conflict episode). Source: best-effort reconstruction from KTU³ (Dietrich-Loretz-Sanmartín 2013) + Smith 1994 Vol 1 + Smith & Pitard 2009 Vol 2 + Pardee 2003 (CoS 1.86) + older PD editions; verification pending against KTU³.
